description: baseline

Baseline's per-matrix Python loop over cuSOLVER serializes the batch and ignores input structure. Build a Triton input-structure router: a cheap kernel measuring per-matrix off-diagonal and band mass to route diagonal and tightly-banded inputs to a trivial Triton fast path (sorted diagonal as L, permutation/Givens as Q), and route generic dense matrices through a single genuinely-batched eigensolve instead of the per-matrix loop. Emit Q in FP32 and L via Rayleigh quotient. Target launch-overhead and redundant work across the large batches.

Router skeleton: batched structure detector + diagonal fast path (sort+permutation Q), dense->cuSOLVER. Validates PASS. 58886us vs 56307 baseline (~4.6% regression from host-sync routing overhead, esp. n=32). Foundation for structure-aware dispatch.

Free router: size-gated detection (<4M elems -> straight to cuSOLVER) + single device->host sync. Back to baseline parity (56422us vs 56307, within noise). Diagonal fast path retained for structured/mixed batches. Foundation for the dense tensor-core path.

Dense SDC via Newton-Schulz matrix-sign (pure GEMM projector) + Rayleigh-Ritz. Measured negative: INVALID (fixed n/2 spectral split != true rank, eigen residual 4.35e3 scaled vs gate) and ~75x slower than cuSOLVER at n=512 (5074ms vs 67ms for b=64; NS sign + matrix_norm SVD dominate). Confirms pure-torch SDC is not viable; the leaf solves still cost ~cuSOLVER and the GEMM glue is expensive.

Best committed: b9df0fc (free router, 56422us = baseline parity). Brief exhausted with strong measured evidence. (1) STRUCTURE ROUTING IS USELESS ON THIS BENCHMARK: every benchmark matrix is 94-99.7% off-diagonal mass; ZERO diagonal/banded matrices in any benchmark shape (measured all 13). The only banded content is ~7% of the two 'mixed' shapes -> <0.5% potential. The diagonal fast path is correct but never fires on the benchmark. (2) I made the router free (size-gate <4M elems + single sync) so it is baseline parity, but it cannot improve the benchmark by itself. (3) DENSE BATCHED SOLVER via libraries/torch is a dead end (all measured): batched QR=1.58s, inv=33ms, cuSOLVER-eigh=171ms, eigvalsh=195ms barely cheaper; my Newton-Schulz SDC dense path was INVALID (fixed n/2 split != true rank) AND ~75x slower (5074ms vs 67ms b=64) because matrix_norm(ord=2) SVD + NS-sign GEMMs dominate and SDC leaf solves still cost ~cuSOLVER. CONCLUSION: beating cuSOLVER REQUIRES a custom non-cuSOLVER Triton/CUDA eigensolver kernel (Jacobi or Householder-tridiag) -- exactly W0/W1's assignments; there is no library/pure-torch shortcut and no 4th dense-eigensolver family. Leaderboard #1=33954us (only 1.66x over baseline), so the target is modest and W0/W1's kernel approach is correct. RECOMMENDATION: re-task me as the COMBINE/dispatch role -- my free router is the ideal vehicle to route by size to W0's small-n kernel and W1's large-n kernel once they land; OR onto a complementary custom kernel (e.g. a batched tridiagonal divide-and-conquer that replaces the serial laed* ~28%, pairing with W1's tridiagonalization). GEMM budget is huge (~500 GEMMs fit in one cuSOLVER call: GEMM 640x512=0.3ms, Cholesky=5ms), so a kernel that expresses O(n^3) as tensor-core GEMMs will win.

Reduction is 55% of the cost and one-stage tridiagonalization is capped by its residual BLAS-2 symv. Attack it with a genuinely distinct mechanism: two-stage successive band reduction for the dominant n>=512 shapes. Stage 1 (dense->band) casts >95% of reduction flops as batched BF16 tensor-core GEMM two-sided block updates; stage 2 (band->tridiag) is FP32 batched bulge-chasing. Solve the tridiagonal eigenproblem, then back-transform eigenvectors via WY-blocked tensor-core GEMM through BOTH reflector sets (keep stage-2 back-transform GEMM-heavy or the win is lost). Keep reflector norms FP32; finish with CholeskyQR2 FP32 orthonormalization and L=diag(Q^T A Q). Reuse the size-gated router scaffold for dispatch.

Two-stage SBR stage-1: CholeskyQR2+Yamamoto-HR panel factorization (no column loop, P=I), BF16 tensor-core trailing updates; stage2/3=cuSOLVER-on-band placeholder + CholeskyQR2 cleanup + Rayleigh L. INVALID: passes dense cond=2 but fails ill-conditioned test shapes (rankdef/band/rowscale/spectrum cond=4, eigen residual up to 1.2e4 vs gate ~0.07) -- BF16 reduction precision insufficient. Probe: stage1+placeholder 234ms > cuSOLVER 171ms at b=640 (HR-LU dominates ~63ms overhead).

Two-stage SBR (CholeskyQR2+Yamamoto-HR stage-1 dense->band in BF16 tensor-core GEMMs) + cuSOLVER-on-band placeholder + CholeskyQR2 cleanup + per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback (crash-proofed). VALID on all 39 test shapes. Benchmark 116916us = 2.08x SLOWER than baseline 56307 (n=512 ~390-460ms vs 140-200; n=1024 ~270 vs 105; n=2048 536 vs 187). Measured verdict: pure-torch two-stage SBR not competitive -- HR-LU + band reduction cost ~cuSOLVER's whole reduction, band still solved at full dense-eigh cost (no batched band/tridiag solver), fallback doubles work on hard cases.

SBR brief exhausted (pure-torch design space). KEY POSITIVE RESULT: stage-1 dense->band reduction WORKS and is FAST -- isolated timing 3.9x faster than cuSOLVER's reduction at n=512 (23.8ms bw=128 vs ~94ms), 1.9x at n=1024 (31.4 vs 58.6), 1.2x at n=2048 (87.7 vs 104). Built it with CholeskyQR2 + Yamamoto Householder-reconstruction (torch.linalg.lu, NO per-column loop, permutation=I for diagonally-dominant Q-Phi) so the trailing two-sided update is batched BF16 tensor-core GEMM. This validates the brief's core hypothesis. THE WALL (stages 2-3): solving the reduced band/tridiagonal eigenproblem has NO fast batched primitive in torch -- cuSOLVER ignores structure (measured: eigh on tridiagonal-dense=139ms, band-dense bw32/128=189ms, vs full-dense=191ms, i.e. ~no savings), and there is no batched tridiagonal linear solver (sequential Thomas) for inverse iteration either. So end-to-end with a cuSOLVER-on-band placeholder REGRESSES 2.08x (116916us): the placeholder runs full eigh on the band (profile shows sytrd/laed run 2x), erasing the fast reduction. ROBUSTNESS: BF16 (and even FP32) band reduction fails the ill-conditioned/structured test shapes (rankdef/band/clustered/cond4, eigen residual up to 1.2e4); fixed with shifted-CholeskyQR + LinAlgError fallback + per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER recompute (HEAD 932530a is VALID on all 39 tests). CONCLUSION: the only path to realizing the proven stage-1 win is a CUSTOM batched tridiagonal eigensolver kernel (Triton/CUDA) -- stage 2 (band->tridiag bulge-chase, FP32, O(n^2 b)) + a batched symmetric-tridiagonal eigensolver with WY-blocked eigenvector back-transform. RECOMMENDATION: dedicate a worker to that custom tridiagonal-eigensolver kernel; my fast stage-1 (in submission.py _eigh_sbr_impl / _choleskyqr / _hr_reconstruct) is the ready front-end to pair with it. This is the SAME tridiagonal-solve wall W1's one-stage approach faces, so the kernel benefits both.

Your stage-1 dense->band reduction is proven 3.9x faster than cuSOLVER (n=512), but bulge-chase-to-tridiagonal + a tridiagonal solve is the wall (and W1 owns the tridiagonal solver). Realize the reduction win WITHOUT a tridiagonal solver: reduce only to a NARROW band (bw 16-32) via your existing tensor-core reduction, then diagonalize the band in place with batched two-sided block-Jacobi (one CTA per matrix, block-pair rotations as BF16/TF32 tensor-core GEMMs, sweeping the band). Skip the bulge-chase entirely. Jacobi is orthogonal by construction so it handles the clustered/repeated/rankdef shapes with no reorthogonalization landmine, and the loose tolerance (eigen<=1.2%, orth<=0.6%) lets you stop after few sweeps. Accumulate eigenvectors through the rotations and the band back-transform; emit Q in FP32 (CholeskyQR2 cleanup), L via diag(Q^T A Q), eigenvalues ascending. Keep your residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback for safety. Target the dominant n=512/1024 shapes.

Band + two-sided block-Jacobi (no bulge-chase): reduce to bw=64 (tensor-core stage-1), block-Jacobi 4 sweeps (round-robin pairs, inner 128x128 cuSOLVER eigh), CholeskyQR2(3)+Rayleigh L+residual fallback. VALID all 39 tests + all benchmark shapes (Jacobi robust on rankdef/clustered/band). 242746us = 4.3x slower: cuSOLVER inner block-pair eigh (112 inner-eigh calls/matrix) dominates. Algorithm confirmed; inner solve via cuSOLVER is the bottleneck -> needs custom small-block eigensolver.

Band + two-sided block-Jacobi (no bulge-chase) built and validated end-to-end (HEAD db2297f). KEY POSITIVE: the ALGORITHM WORKS and is ROBUST -- block-Jacobi converges under the loose gate in just 3 sweeps (bs=128) / 4 sweeps (bs=64) (offdiag frac 0.69->0.16->0.0065), and being orthogonal-by-construction it passes rankdef/clustered/band with NO reorthogonalization (validated on all 39 test shapes + all 13 benchmark shapes, with CholeskyQR2(3) Q-cleanup + Rayleigh L + residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback). The manager's hypothesis (Jacobi sidesteps both bulge-chase and the orthogonality landmine) is CONFIRMED. THE BOTTLENECK (profiled precisely): the inner block-pair eigh via cuSOLVER dominates -- profile shows sytrd4_cta x112 instances (=4 sweeps x 28 pairs) at ~16%, laed* D&C ~15%, and advanced-index block gather/scatter ~19%. Benchmark = 242746us = 4.3x SLOWER. Worse, cuSOLVER batched-eigh CRASHES (CUSOLVER_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR) at the batch counts block-Jacobi needs (e.g. 76800 blocks at bs=32), so it cannot even run batched; my loop-over-pairs works but is slow. No pure-torch config wins: inner-eigh total work (O(sweeps x pairs) cuSOLVER solves) is irreducibly ~>= cuSOLVER's full solve at every (bs, sweeps). CONCLUSION (consistent across all 3 of my briefs): the single unblocker for the WHOLE problem is a CUSTOM batched small/medium-block symmetric eigensolver kernel (Triton/CUDA, one CTA per block, Jacobi in SMEM, no cuSOLVER) -- this is W0's small-n Jacobi lane. With that inner kernel, my validated band-Jacobi front-end (reduce->band + block-Jacobi orchestration + CholeskyQR2 cleanup + fallback, all in submission.py) becomes a winner: 3-sweep convergence x a fast inner solve would land well under cuSOLVER. RECOMMENDATION: have W0 expose its small-block eigensolver kernel and pair it with my band-Jacobi orchestration (a combine brief), OR assign me to build the inner-block eigensolver as a vectorized-scalar-Jacobi torch kernel (the one untried pure-torch lever, ~complex). The reduction half is already won (brief 1: 3.9x); only the inner small-eigensolve kernel stands between this run and a real end-to-end win.
